Define corporate social responsibility. State and discuss the meaning, three circles of
corporate responsibilities, and benefits of corporate social responsibility in the theme
of Business Ethics, considering the quote: “Profit is not an end itself, but a means of
encouraging and rewarding hard work of employees, executives and managers and
investment of owners and stockholders; building a better business, and serving society
better.”

Should there be teacher-student friendship? Should the teacher advocate views in the
class? Yes, or No. Discuss. [You may answer these two questions following the
prescribed details of the theme of education ethics.]

You may answer the following question in the given situation, keeping in view your
understanding of the ethical use of the four categories of professional information in
engineering: An automobile engineer, Malavika, resigned from her job at Hyundai
Motor India Limited on May 14, 2025, and joined Tata Motors, India on May 15,
2025. Given this job change, what should be her ethical response to sharing or
protecting professional information at Tata Motors, India or elsewhere that she
acquired at Hyundai Motor India Limited? [It may help you to know that automobile
engineering is a specialized field that focuses on vehicle design, development, and
maintenance. It encompasses various aspects of vehicle technology, including
mechanical, electrical, and electronic systems. Automobile engineers work on
everything from the combustion engines and transmissions to modern vehicles'
sophisticated software and safety features.]

When Mapping the World Crosses a Line
Between 2007 and 2010, Google's Street View cars, which were driving around the
world taking photographs for Google Maps, were also collecting data from unsecured
Wi-Fi networks without the knowledge or consent of the people using them.
This data included personal information such as emails, passwords, browsing history,
and other private communications from homes and businesses. Google later admitted
that the data collection was a mistake caused by code written by one of its engineers.
However, internal emails revealed that some Google employees knew the data was
being collected.
Once the activity came to light in 2010, several governments launched investigations,
and Google was fined in multiple countries. Privacy regulators in Germany, Canada,
the U.S., and the U.K. criticized Google for collecting sensitive personal data without
permission, even if the networks were “open.” The criticisms of privacy regulators
were based on the following ethical questions: Can a company claim data collection is
accidental when it involves sensitive private information? Does having an unsecured
Wi-Fi network mean people "deserve" to have their data collected? What
responsibility does a company have to audit and monitor its data-gathering practices?
Should large companies be treated differently because of their size and reach?
Do you agree with the privacy regulators? Even if someone leaves their Wi-Fi
network unsecured, is it ethical for a company to collect their data without telling
them? Why or why not? Examine whether "technical accessibility" equals ethical
permission. What ethical safeguards should a company like Google have to prevent
unintentional privacy violations by its employees or systems? [Use theoretical
details of the ethical issue of “Privacy, Security, and Moral Wrong Doing” in
the theme of Computer Ethics, and an ethical theory of your choice to discuss
the case and respond to the questions given above.]

Discuss in brief the ethical basis of Whistle-blowing. Describe and analyze the six conditions for
justified whistle-blowing. You may use examples to strengthen your answer.

Describe and analyze the profit motive in Business Ethics and discuss with the help from the
prescribed study material the arguments for and against “Corporate Social Responsibility.” You
may conclude the answer with your own assessment.

The Ethics of Pharmaceutical Marketing
Peggy Connolly, Ruth Ann Althaus, Robert Boyd Skipper
Pharmaceutical companies spend billions of dollars annually to research, develop, and market
drugs. According to the Pew Charitable Trust, the pharmaceutical industry spent over $27 billion
on marketing alone in 2012, with $24 billion of that devoted to marketing to physicians. The
Economist (3/2/2013) reported a Deloitte survey showing that 35 percent of doctors accept food,
entertainment, or travel from the pharmaceutical industry, and 16 percent accept consulting or
speaking fees. The Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education reports that
pharmaceutical and medical device companies sponsored almost one-third of continuing medical
education (CME) opportunities for doctors in 2011.
Observers worry about whether physicians can be objective in selecting and prescribing drugs
when they are plied with free samples, gifts, speaking and consulting fees, and free CME. Critics
worry that persuasive and persistent sales representatives (who are not trained in medicine) have
highly sophisticated marketing techniques and strong financial motivation to sell their company's
drugs. The Georgetown University Medical Center reports that 16 percent of doctors change
their prescribing practices after one minute with a sales rep and 52 percent change after three
minutes. Doctors' insistent denials of being influenced by drug reps are belied by the success of
the industry's marketing efforts.
Given the complexity and ever-changing nature of medicines, some experts assert that
information doctors gain from pharmaceutical companies' efforts is valuable enough to outweigh
the documented higher cost to consumers and the possibility of bias in doctors' prescribing
habits.
Do you find the marketing techniques and efforts of pharmaceutical companies ethical?
You may answer the question regarding the case considering your understanding of the topic
“Marketing Ethics” in the theme of Business Ethics and any one theoretical framework of ethics.

State and discuss the Kantian justification of proposed solutions to women and family issues in
the workplace, namely the pay gap and glass ceiling, conflicting demands of family life and work
life, and the second-shift problem. You may conclude the answer with your assessment.

Describe and analyse the profit motive in Business Ethics. Discuss three circles of corporate
responsibilities and examples of “Corporate Social Responsibility” with the help of the
prescribed study material. You may conclude the answer with a small critical note.

A work practice is a part of company culture
Clare Bartlett
Tara was recently promoted to a managerial position at her industrial engineering company. With
her new position, she is now responsible for overseeing the company’s production factory,
meaning approximately 50 factory workers now report to her. Although Tara previously worked
as an engineer and has no experience running a factory, she is excited to begin her new position.
At the end of her first day, Tara is confused to see her factory workers continuing to work well
past the end of their 8-hour shift. She then goes to the factory supervisor (who reports to her) to
express concern because the factory does not have the budget to pay overtime to so many
workers. The supervisor smiles at Tara and explains that the factory meets production goals by
making the factory workers work off the clock. The workers knew this expectation and followed
it to keep their jobs. Tara is shocked to learn this practice has become part of the company
culture, but the supervisor explains that the company’s CEO (Tara’s boss) is aware of this
expectation.
Do you agree with the factory supervisor or Tara? What should Tara do? Explain and discuss.
You may respond to the questions regarding the case considering your understanding of the topic
“Employer-employee Relations” and any one theoretical framework of ethics.

State and discuss the reasons for a professional to accept the need for ethics in professions particularly
when already there are formal rules existing in his workplace to help him to act ethically and legally for
the common good. You may conclude the answer with your own brief critical assessment.

Define Business Ethics. Describe in brief the reasons for keeping Business Ethics as a part of study of
Professional Ethics. State and analyze any three lessons that you consider you may draw as a business
professional from your understanding of Indian Ethics to work as an ethical business professional in a
business company? Invent details of a problem situation to elaborate your answer.

Apathy over Anonymity: The Ethics of Employer-employee Relation
Nabilah Deen
Sanya works in a research facility that provides statistical results for the bioengineering firm
TechCureCase. She is one of four interns expected to go through hundreds of samples per day. At her
first week on the job, her supervisor informs her that all blood samples are to be completely anonymous.
No testing can be done if personal information is revealed—meaning, the samples must be properly
disposed of if opened, or returned to the physicians if unopened to be re-anonymized.
For the first five weeks, most of the new interns follow procedures to check that samples were
anonymized before testing occurred. However, one of the interns, Manpreet, failed to verify whether the
samples were anonymized. Halfway through the testing, Sanya discovers the non-anonymized samples.
She considers whether they should tell their supervisor, but the other interns ask her not to speak up so
that they will not get in trouble. One of the interns argues that if they remove the information from the
non-anonymized samples, the batch would otherwise be fine. Manpreet is hesitant to go to their
supervisor as it is his fault, but Sanya can see that neither does supervisor like the idea the other interns
are suggesting.
What should Sanya do? Do you find the behavior of interns as employees of supervisor ethical? Discuss.
You may answer the questions regarding the case considering your understanding of the topic
“Employer-employee Relation” in Professional Ethics and any one theoretical framework of ethics.

Why ethics is needed for professions when there are formal rules in place to guide the
professionals working in business organizations? You may respond to the question
with the help of two reasons to establish the need of ethics for professions and you
may also elaborate your answer with reference to three standards of ethical inquiry.

Define marketing ethics and advertising ethics. State and analyze three issues of
advertising ethics: Deceptive Advertising, Irrational Persuasion, Impact of
Advertising. You may conclude the answer with your own brief assessment.

Write a brief note on the areas and forms of discrimination. State and discuss the three
ethical arguments against discrimination in a workplace to negate the importance of
forms of discrimination. You may use examples to elaborate your answer.

May the Truth be with You
Jocelyn Tan
Catherine is a new hire at a startup that produces LCD displays for large venues, such as shopping malls. Part of her job requires her to troubleshoot malfunctioning displays.
One day, a shopping mall reported that two display units out of twelve had stopped working from their installation three months prior. The customer also noted serial and revision numbers on the two units were different from the rest of the units.
At the job site, Catherine inspected the displays and realized her company had sold units that were from a bad batch (i.e. group of displays that did not have over 50%
yield during manufacturing). Catherine wanted to tell the site why the units failed, but
recognized that if she disclosed this information, the site would be eligible to receive
replacement displays at no additional cost. On the other hand, if she blamed the
failing units on a weaker cause, such as improper installation, her company would be
able to charge the site for replacement units.
Catherine knew her manager would want her to choose the option that would
minimize the company’s losses; however, she wanted to be honest with the site as
they were one of the company’s best customers.
What should she do?
You may answer the question regarding the case considering your understanding of
the topic “Standards and Values for an Engineer” in the theme of Engineering Ethics
and any one theoretical framework of ethics. If you want to include any detail from
any other topic or theme, you may have one, but that would be treated as optional and
additional to the suggested topic and theme.

“Women professionals experience adversities in the workplace, such as sexual
stereotypes, sexual harassment, the pay gap, and the glass ceiling. In addition, they
face the challenges of combining full-time work with family obligations.” Discuss.

Define Corporate Social Responsibility. State and discuss the three circles of
corporate responsibility focusing especially on third circle, namely corporate social
responsibility with an examination of arguments for and against corporate social
responsibility.

An engineer, Pratyush, resigned from his job at CEAT Tyres on April 12, 2024, and
joined MRF Tyres on April 13, 2024. In view of this change in job, what should be
his ethical response to revealing or sharing professional information at MRF or
elsewhere that he acquired at CEAT? You may discuss his ethical response with
reference to four categories of professional information and conclude with your
critical assessment.

Social Networking App and Privacy: An Ethics Case Study
Irina Raicu
Path is a social networking app that describes itself as "the smart journal that helps
you share life with the ones you love." The company behind it was founded in 2010
by Dave Morin, who had previously worked at Facebook. In February 2012, Path
found itself at the center of a privacy controversy after a Singapore-based blogger
Arun Thampi reported that the app collected all the information in its users'
"Contacts" lists, without asking the users' permission to do so. As it turned out, that
information, unencrypted, was transmitted to Path's servers, where it was stored-again
unencrypted.
Initially, the founder of Path responded in comments to Arun Thampi's blog by
stating, "We upload the address book to our servers in order to help the user find and
connect to their friends and family on Path quickly and efficiently as well as to notify
them when friends and family join Path;" he added that his company's actions were an
"industry best practice." Other commenters also noted that many other apps were
similarly downloading users' contact information without notifying the users or asking
for permission.
Was it unethical for the Path developers to collect and store the app users' "Contacts"
information in the way they did? Was the company's response an appropriate and
sufficient resolution of Path's practices? What should Path's designers have done?
You may answer the questions regarding the case considering your understanding of
the topic “Privacy, Security, and Moral Wrong Doing” in the theme of Computer
Ethics and any one theoretical framework of ethics. If you want to include any detail
from any other topic or theme, you may have one, but that would be treated as
optional and additional to the suggested topic and theme.

State and briefly discuss the nature of and relation between Professional Ethics and Business Ethics.
What should be the appropriate ethical behaviour of a business professional regarding the issues of
Sales Practices in Marketing Ethics and Deceptive Advertising in Advertising Ethics? Discuss.

What is Discrimination in Professional Ethics? Describe the areas and forms of Discrimination,
along with elaborating three ethical arguments against Discrimination. You may conclude with a
brief response to the observation: determining what constitutes discrimination can be challenging.

Define Privacy in Computer Ethics. State and discuss the issue of Privacy on the Internet with a
focus on five principles for protecting privacy. Suggest a value-oriented intervention to prevent the
possible violations of privacy on the internet.

“Have you said anything to your wife about this? Your decision will affect her as much as it will
affect you. And what about your kids? Have you thought about how it might affect them? You may
have to move. And what about your family’s needs? They have become accustomed to a certain kind
of life. If you move ahead and blow the whistle, everything will change. You may never even work
in the industry again. Think about all your education, about your plans and goals.” Mohit is trying to
talk some sense into his friend, Srinivas, who has discovered that the managers of his bicycle
manufacturing company knowingly let a product on the market with a defect. The defect is beginning
to hurt people, mainly children. Further, his friend has discovered that the problem could be solved
with a relatively inexpensive part costing Rs. 200. Since there are no government or industry
standards, the company will wait until forced by the government to attend to the defect, thinking that
this is the more profitable move. Mohit’s friend thinks bringing this to the public's attention is his
duty. The situation is also complicated because the product design employs a trade secret. Srinivas
knows that if he has to go public with this information, he may be required to prove his case, which
can be done only by revealing the trade secret. Having seen this situation before, Mohit knows that
his friend will be fired and will almost certainly never work again as an engineer because of his
reputation as a whistleblower.
Many people would argue that Mohit’s friend has a moral duty to blow the whistle on the company
and its managers. What reasons are there to do this?
Mohit’s friend has a family. Nevertheless, he still wants to blow the whistle. Should his friend
consider the impact his decision will have on his family? In this case, are his family obligations
morally relevant? How should he weigh his obligations to the public against his obligations to his
family?
[Use theoretical details of ethical issues of “Whistle-blowing” and “Professional Information
in Engineering” and an ethical theory of your choice to answer the questions.]

Define profession. What are the six features of the profession as a working concept? You may
provide details of features and discuss the possible interconnectivity of these six features.

Define ethics. State and discuss the Aristotelian perspective of virtue ethics, especially regarding
his response to three questions: What does it mean to be a good human being? What the function
of a human being is supposed to be? How are human beings supposed to use their rationality?

Describe and analyze any three fundamental ideas of Business Ethics of your choice from the
prescribed study material with special reference to the topic of “Corporate Social
Responsibility.” You may conclude the answer with a critical assessment.
